description: Sapele is a reddish-brown African hardwood related to mahogany, known for a striking ribbon stripe on quarter-sawn faces. It is used for furniture, cabinetry, doors, flooring, veneer, plywood and guitar backs and sides.

hazards.summary: The UK safety regulator lists skin irritation among the reported effects of sapele.

A Spanish case report describes a carpenter with work-related asthma from sapele dust, and a peer-reviewed review lists sapele among woods that cause occupational asthma. We have not yet confirmed what testing the case report used.
The same Spanish report describes an allergic skin reaction to sapele dust alongside the asthma.
IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nasal cavity and sinuses after long-term exposure.

related_species_note: Sapele is in the same family (Meliaceae) as genuine mahogany, African mahogany and utile (Entandrophragma utile); evidence for those woods is listed separately.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed sapele (Entandrophragma cylindricum) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Heartwood a medium to deep reddish-brown with a slight purple tone, uniform across the face; no visible sapwood. Quarter-sawn face with tightly interlocked grain producing a bold, regular ribbon stripe of alternating light and dark bands that shift as the light changes, fine even texture, small pores, and a high natural luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed quarter-sawn board of sapele with reddish-brown heartwood and a bold ribbon stripe of alternating light and dark bands.
notes_internal: AlvarezCuesta-2004 title reports occupational asthma and IgE-mediated contact dermatitis from sapele, but there is no PubMed abstract and we could not access the full text; if it includes a specific inhalation challenge, prick test or sIgE, upgrade asthma and skin hazards to level 1. Schlunssen-2018 Table 1 lists sapele OA citing Kersten 1994 and Oertmann 1993 (German, Allergologie; not in PubMed).
